Five-color · Prepare reanimator · Bracket 3

Codie, Ravenous Codex · Prepared Reanimator

A five-color reanimator deck for Codie, Ravenous Codex, brewed and tested in the mtg-gauntlet simulator. The deck tab covers how it plays, its win conditions, the decklist and the rulings to know; the gauntlet tab covers how it performed.

The deck

29.7%games won (fair share 25%)
22.7%best-of-3 series won (fair share ~16%)
3 / 3Game Changers · Bracket 3

Fill your graveyard with huge creatures, then cast reanimation spells from prepare creatures. Codie copies every prepared spell you cast, so one Reanimate brings back two threats. You win in combat with fatties your opponents can't keep answering, and drain triggers finish off the last points.

Game plan

  1. Turns 1–3: set up. Mana dorks, rocks and cheap preparers. Put a fatty in the graveyard with Entomb, Buried Alive, Stitcher's Supplier, Faithless Looting, or the copied Omit Variables mill (Paradox Shaper, Theorix Metamage, Void Extrapolator). Codie on turn 3, with Boots or Greaves when you can.
  2. Turns 3–5: start reanimating. Animate Dead, Necromancy, Reanimate and Exhume from hand. Prepared Reanimate (Grave Researcher), Bind to Life (Vastlands Scavenger) and Restore Relic (Lorehold Archivist) each get copied by Codie, so you get two threats per spell.
  3. Turn 6+: snowball. Paradox Shaper re-prepares every upkeep. Skycoach Conductor flickers a preparer to re-arm it. Codie's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, {T} re-prepares the whole board. Elesh Norn or Massacre Wurm clears the way, and Gray Merchant drains the rest.

What to watch for

  • The deck is slow. Wins come around turn 14, losses around turn 10. Mulligan hands with no early mana or no way to fill the graveyard.
  • Codie is the multiplier. In games where it copies 6+ spells you win 55–61% of the time; with fewer than 3 copies, 17%. Protect it before you go all in.
  • Hard matchups: fast typal and aggro decks (13%), and lifegain combo (Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond). Save Assassin's Trophy and Beast Within for their enchantments.

Core engine

The commander and the six prepare creatures the deck runs on. Each one's spell gets copied by Codie.

Rulings to know

The interactions this deck runs into most, with Comprehensive Rules references (2025-09-19 edition on the mtg-rules server). Prepare is rule 722, new with Secrets of Strixhaven. Tap a ruling to open it.

Prepare & Codie

A prepared spell is a copy you cast from exile.

When a creature becomes prepared, a copy of its prepare spell is created in exile, and you may cast that copy. Because it's cast from exile, it counts as "cast from anywhere other than your hand", so Vega, the Watcher draws you a card.

CR 722.3c, 707.12
Normal timing applies.

Prepare spells follow their own card type. The instants (Bind to Life, Ancestral Recall, Swords to Plowshares, Lightning Bolt) can be cast any time you have priority. The sorceries (Reanimate, Restore Relic, Omit Variables, Demonic Tutor, Regrowth) need your main phase with an empty stack.

CR 117.1a
The creature unprepares the moment the spell is cast.

If the prepare spell gets countered, the creature stays unprepared. You don't get it back.

CR 722.3c, 601.2i
Codie's copy is not cast.

It doesn't trigger Codie again, so there's no loop, and it doesn't trigger Vega. It does trigger Archmage Emeritus ("cast or copy"). The copy can take new targets, it counts as a prepare spell itself, and it goes on the stack above the original, so it resolves first.

CR 707.10, 707.10c, 722.3d
Codie's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} ability needs {T}.

Codie is a creature, so it can't use the ability the turn it enters unless it has haste. Swiftfoot Boots and Lightning Greaves both give haste. The ability only prepares creatures that have a prepare spell and aren't already prepared.

CR 722.3a, 302.6
Leaving the battlefield resets prepared.

A flickered creature returns as a new object. Creatures that "enter prepared" come back ready again, so Skycoach Conductor's All Aboard on Vastlands Scavenger or Emeritus of Woe re-arms its spell.

CR 400.7, 722.3a

Reanimation

A copied Reanimate is two separate spells.

The copy and the original can each take a creature from any graveyard, and you lose life equal to the mana value of each creature. Archon (8) plus Atraxa (7) costs 15 of your 40 life.

CR 707.10c
Animate Dead's creature gets -1/-0.

If Animate Dead leaves the battlefield, for example to enchantment removal, you sacrifice the creature. Necromancy works the same way.

CR Card text
Necromancy at instant speed is temporary.

Cast it during an opponent's turn or in combat (a surprise blocker, or stealing a creature from a graveyard) and you sacrifice the creature at the next cleanup step. Cast it at sorcery speed if you want to keep the creature.

CR Card text
Persist only returns nonlegendary creatures.

Atraxa, Elesh Norn and Sheoldred are legendary, so Persist can't get them. Its targets are Archon, the Titans, Massacre Wurm, Terror and Gray Merchant, which come back with a -1/-1 counter.

CR Card text
Living Death exiles first, then sacrifices.

The creatures you sacrifice reach the graveyard after the exile step, so they don't come back this time. That includes your preparers, so count both sides before casting it.

CR Card text
Exhume lets every player choose.

Choices are made in turn order starting with the active player, and each player sees the earlier choices. A player with no creature in their graveyard gets nothing.

CR 101.4

Win conditions

Gray Merchant counts devotion when it resolves.

Devotion counts every black mana symbol in the mana costs of permanents you control. That includes Gray Merchant's own {B}{B}, creatures you reanimated (their mana cost still exists even though you didn't pay it), and hybrid {U/B} on Paradox Shaper and Theorix Metamage. Codie ({3}) adds nothing.

CR 700.5
Terror of the Peaks triggers for every creature that enters.

That includes Grave Titan's zombie tokens (2 damage each). The damage uses the creature's power when the trigger resolves, so Elesh Norn's +2/+2 adds 2 to each trigger.

CR 603.2, 608.2h
Elesh Norn's -2/-2 is permanent while she's out.

Opposing creatures with 2 or less toughness die right away (a state-based action), and so do new ones as they enter.

CR 704.5f, 613.4
Archon's opponent chooses what to sacrifice.

It's an edict, not targeted removal, so they'll sacrifice their worst creature. It still gets past hexproof and indestructible.

CR 701.21a
Atraxa only sees prepare creatures as creatures.

In the library, preparation cards have only their creature characteristics, so Atraxa can't take a preparer as the "sorcery" or "instant" pick.

CR 722.4

Protection & interaction

Lightning Greaves gives shroud, which stops your own targeting too.

With Greaves on a creature, All Aboard (Skycoach Conductor) can't flicker it. Swiftfoot Boots gives hexproof, which only stops opponents. Keep Greaves on Codie and Boots on anything you plan to flicker. Greaves' equip costs {0}, so you can move it off first.

CR 702.18a, 702.11b
Crippling Fear: name the type on resolution. Wizard is the right call.

Naming Wizard spares Paradox Shaper, Theorix Metamage, Variable Chaser, Emeritus of Ideation, Archmage Emeritus, Studious First-Year and Emeritus of Conflict. Codie (1/4) and your fatties survive -3/-3 anyway.

CR Card text
Cyclonic Rift's overload doesn't target.

It hits hexproof and shroud creatures, which makes it the answer to opposing Voltron.

CR 702.96, 115.10
Aetherize only bounces attacking creatures.

Tokens returned to hand cease to exist. Cast it after attackers are declared, before damage.

CR 111.7, 704.5d

Predictions vs results

  • A, weak to Storm, Control and Stax: held. 19.2%, 19.6% and 15.7%, each 5 to 6 points under the baseline.
  • A, interaction would fix the creature matchups: missed. Tokens, Typal and Aggro all got worse. A lands more infinite-combo kills than the baseline (3,757 vs 3,436), but its combat kills fall from 2,594 to 867. The baseline's prepare bodies were winning games in combat, and removal didn't replace that.
  • B, weak to Reanimator: partly held. 24.6%, below its own average but 3 points above the baseline. Opposing Living Death wipes it 151 times.
  • B, weak to Control: missed. 30.1% / 23.0%, B's biggest gain (+6 games). Recursive threats come back after wipes; combo pieces don't.
  • B, weak to Aristocrats: held. 15.9% / 7.3%. Edicts and drains blunt big single threats.
  • Surprise: Lifegain is B's worst category at 5.8% with 0 series won. Amalia Benavides Aguirre wipes the board 347 times in 647 games, which looks like a simulator outlier worth checking.

Swap test on B (300 series, paired shuffles)

  • Etali, Primal Conqueror → Gray Merchant of Asphodel: kept. +2.0 games and +2.3 series overall; +4.9 Turbo combo, +5.3 Enchantress, +4.2 Typal, +3.7 Control; no category worse by 3 or more.
  • Boros Charm → Kozilek's Return: −0.2 overall (+4.6 Typal, −3.3 Storm). Not kept.
  • Heroic Intervention → Ashen Rider: −0.2 overall (+3.9 Typal, −3.9 Artifacts). Not kept.

The baseline was rerun after the engine change because opponents' Animate Dead, Entomb, Faithless Looting and similar cards now work too. That lowered the baseline from 23.6% to 21.4% mean games, with the biggest drops in Turbo combo, Reanimator and Artifacts.

Package tests for the weak matchups (Oct 4)

Two packages aimed at the six weak categories (★), plus both together, at 100 best-of-3 series per category on a fixed engine. At 100 series a single category moves about ±2.8 points between runs, so read single-category differences under 4 points as noise. The 18-category means are much steadier.

  • Defensive: Swiftfoot Boots and Lightning Greaves (for Boros Charm and Fact or Fiction) protect Codie. Aetherize (for Harmonized Trio) and Crippling Fear naming Wizard (for Austere Command) answer wide boards.
  • Tempo: Exhume for Unburial Rites. Tutors fetch Elesh Norn first, and Entomb fires early when a reanimation spell is already in hand, binning Elesh, Atraxa or Archon.

What it shows

  • The combined list wins: 29.7% of games and 22.7% of series, against 25.2% / 17.5% for the previous list. It's now the list in this report.
  • Defensive does what it was built for. Tokens rise from 14.3% to 22.5%, Landfall from 16.5% to 24.7%, and Blink and Aristocrats each gain about 5 points. Codie is removed 18% less often.
  • Tempo mostly helps the matchups that were already fine: Turbo combo +7.7, Storm +7.2, Artifacts +7.2. Getting a fatty down a turn earlier wins races.
  • Typal didn't move (13–16% in every build). The Ur-Dragon, Lathril and Shilgengar win in combat before any of these cards matter. It needs a different answer, likely a cheaper sweeper.
  • Lifegain is still low at 13.4% after the Amalia fix. The losses are now real infinite combos (Liesa, Dina, Oloro, Exquisite Blood), not a simulator bug.
  • Watch Voltron (35.0% to 26.5%) and Reanimator (31.0% to 26.7%) on the combined list. Both drops are larger than the noise, and a likely cause is Exhume handing opponents their best creature back.

Engine changes for this round: Amalia Benavides Aguirre no longer wipes the board when cast (it only does so at exactly 20 power), self-mill stops below 25 cards in the library, and Crippling Fear, Exhume and the Entomb pilot options are now modeled. The "Previous list" column is a rerun on that fixed engine, so the comparison is fair.

How this was run

  • Opponents are EDHREC average decklists, using both the Upgraded (bracket 3) and Optimized (bracket 4) versions. Each series rolls each opponent's bracket at random and keeps it for all three games.
  • Every card in every deck was tagged from its real rules text (Forge card scripts): mana, removal, wipes, counterspells, stax effects, tokens, anthems, drains, combos and alternate wins. Opponents play the cards they actually draw.
  • Seat order is random each game. A game that hits 25 rounds counts as a draw, which counts as a loss for the series.
  • Limits: decisions are rule-based, not expert play. Politics, deals and bluffs don't exist, and some cards are simplified. Treat the matchup shape as the finding, not the exact percentages.
